blockers.quote: The first words, yours, from a second before: "I'll forget it all after anyway", cramming as always, the tea already in her hand.
blockers.why: story #9: The cost is being unable to forgive your mother, but the opening habit is only cramming and forgetting exam material. The cost does not attack that habit.
blockers.fix: Establish interpersonal forgetting in the opening: Mom snaps "Again?" as she sets down the tea; as usual, the irritation is already fading when you say, "I'll forget it all after anyway." Then the power restores both the pages and her age-nine shout.

blockers.quote: At eighty, the shout from age nine is as loud as this morning, and so is the morning she taught you to ride a cycle.
blockers.why: story #5: The second jump ends with an argument, then the outline simply jumps to age eighty. The beats currently join as "and then," without a causal turn.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "Because you keep using perfect recall as evidence against her, each new kindness must fight the old shout at full volume. The years accelerate. At eighty, the shout remains—but so does the morning she taught you to ride a cycle."

suggestions.quote: Then the second fact, landing on your replay within two lines: people who remember almost every day of their lives, and Jill Price's own words about living the old fights again
suggestions.fix: Use one compact fact: identify Jill Price and give one short quote, then immediately show your replay. Move the general memory explanation earlier or cut it.

suggestions.quote: Do I remember from before the power? Can I still learn new things? Will I go mad?
suggestions.fix: Mark the first as answered by line 34. In the exam beat, answer learning with: "New pages stay. Knowing what to do with them does not." Show that you still function without making or answering a mental-health diagnosis.

suggestions.quote: Does mom remember it too? Is there a cure?
suggestions.fix: Mom's memory is answered in line 37. Add "There is no off switch" to the rule beat before 0:30 so the cure question is answered without introducing a late power rule.

suggestions.quote: The choice at about 78%: you remember both; which one gets the last word tonight?
suggestions.fix: Name this as the moving wordless peak: hold 8 seconds while the shout and cycle memory compete, with the pages shifting every 2–4 seconds; then show your choice immediately.

keep.quote: I'll forget it all after anyway
Then the question quotes no page; it asks you to apply one to something new, and you freeze.
She doesn't remember the shout. You do. The tea's still warm.
